summary: Curated collection of 2026 AI agent research papers covering agent engineering, memory, evaluation, workflows, and autonomous systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — useful reference index but no specific actionable gap surfaced beyond what is already tracked in the open backlog.

summary: Technical survey covering self-improvement paradigms for LLMs including feedback loops, reflection, and iterative plan refinement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — themes (plan repair, episodic retry) already tracked by open issues HID-186 (partial retry) and HID-188 (episodic memory). No net-new gap.

source: Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops (arXiv 2607.07663)
summary: Explores recursive self-improvement from bounded self-refinement to fully autonomous research loops with meta-learning from failures.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — interesting framing of self-improvement tiers but nothing AgentForge uniquely lacks beyond open issues HID-186 and HID-188. The autonomous research loop angle is covered by HID-72 auto-dispatch.

summary: Open-source tool that runs ML experiments in a loop, retaining only improvements over the current best. 700 experiments across two days, full lineage in Git.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — strong signal for automated dispatch loops and improvement tracking, but HID-72 (auto-dispatch) and HID-186 (plan repair) already cover the core capability. Skill distillation (shipped) handles lineage.

summary: Karpathy proposes compiling raw materials once into a persistent structured Markdown wiki instead of live RAG, enabling accumulated knowledge across agent runs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — maps to skill distillation which is already shipped in AgentForge (distillationAgent.ts, agentSkillRepository.ts). The executor-prompt injection gap is tracked by HID-188.

summary: Architecture document with 9 rules shifting execution and bookkeeping to AI models, enabling autonomous agents through loops, planning, generation, review, and state management on disk.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge already follows loop/planning/review/state-machine patterns. No new gap identified.

source: LangGraph v0.4 with PostgresSaver and streaming tool-output API
summary: LangGraph v0.4 ships improved state persistence with PostgresSaver checkpointer and streaming tool-output API; human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — state persistence and checkpointing is the same capability area as HID-186 (stage-level partial retry via earliest-failure-point detection). No new issue warranted.

source: CrewAI 0.95 with memory backend abstraction and async crew runner

relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has skill distillation (shipped) and episodic memory is tracked by HID-188. Memory backend abstraction pattern noted for future reference.

source: AutoGen 1.0 / Microsoft Agent Framework strategic pivot

relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AutoGen's conversational multi-agent model doesn't map to AgentForge's CLI subprocess pattern. Microsoft's pivot away is noted.

source: POLARIS governed orchestration framework (DAG + rubric-guided selection)

relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the rubric-guided selection aspect is interesting for plan evaluation but AgentForge's policyEngine.ts already provides validator-gated execution. No verified missing part beyond adversarial plan critique (HID-93).
